title: Predicting the Dynamics of Complex System via Multiscale Diffusion Autoencoder

problem.claim: Accurate prediction of complex-system dynamics requires models that capture intrinsic dynamics.

gap.claim: Existing methods encode low-dimensional latent spaces but overlook the inherent multiscale structure of complex systems, limiting accurate prediction of complex spatiotemporal evolution.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Multiscale Diffusion Prediction Network that uses multiscale structure to discover the latent space of intrinsic dynamics.
The method encodes multiscale features through a multiscale diffusion autoencoder to guide diffusion-based reconstruction.
The method introduces an attention-based graph neural ordinary differential equation to model co-evolution across scales.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluations on representative systems.
The authors report a 53.23% average prediction-error reduction compared with baselines.
The authors report superior robustness and generalization.

narrative_sequence.summary: Predicting complex-system dynamics is important for scientific and engineering applications.
Prediction accuracy depends on capturing intrinsic dynamics.
Existing latent-space methods overlook multiscale structure and struggle with complex spatiotemporal evolution.

The proposed network discovers intrinsic-dynamics latent structure using multiscale diffusion encoding and models cross-scale co-evolution with an attention-based graph neural ordinary differential equation.
Evaluations on representative systems are reported to show lower prediction error, robustness, and generalization.

source_observation.claim: Existing methods may miss important structure when they represent complex systems only through low-dimensional latent spaces.

interpretation.claim: For multiscale dynamical data, explicitly representing interactions across scales may improve predictive modeling.

application.claim: When designing predictors for complex spatiotemporal systems, consider multiscale feature encoding and cross-scale dynamics modeling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach benefits systems lacking meaningful multiscale structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated representative systems.
The abstract does not provide baseline identities, evaluation protocols, or error definitions.
The abstract does not report ablations or independent verification of the claimed robustness and generalization.
